title: MUZZLE: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Web Agents Against Indirect Prompt Injection Attacks
reason: The official abstract presents and evaluates an LLM-specific, trajectory-guided red-teaming framework for indirect prompt injection against web agents.
contribution: Introduces trajectory-guided adaptive red-teaming that finds indirect prompt-injection surfaces and refines attacks against executing web agents.

title: Connect the Dots: Knowledge Graph–Guided Crawler Attack on Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
reason: The official abstract studies knowledge-base extraction from deployed RAG systems and evaluates a concrete adaptive attack; the primary object is security of LLM-integrated software.
contribution: Formulates RAG knowledge-base stealing as adaptive coverage and introduces a knowledge-graph-guided crawler attack evaluated across corpora and generators.

title: Security-Aware Sensor Fusion with MATE: the Multi-Agent Trust Estimator.
reason: The paper's abstract describes Bayesian trust estimation for adversarial sensor fusion in cyber-physical multi-agent networks; it does not use an LLM or study LLM-integrated software.

title: DCMI: A Differential Calibration Membership Inference Attack Against Retrieval-Augmented Generation.
reason: The abstract presents a membership-inference attack against RAG knowledge stores and validates it on deployed RAG platforms, directly studying security of LLM-integrated software.
contribution: Introduces differential calibration for membership inference against RAG knowledge stores and evaluates the attack on research and deployed RAG systems.

title: Augmenting Search-based Program Synthesis with Local Inference Rules to Improve Black-box Deobfuscation.
reason: The author-supplied abstract and paper describe search-based symbolic program synthesis for black-box deobfuscation without an LLM or foundation-model method.

title: SAGA: A Security Architecture for Governing AI Agentic Systems.
reason: The official abstract proposes and evaluates an access-control and cryptographic-token architecture specifically for interacting LLM agents.
contribution: Introduces a governance architecture with user-defined access policies and cryptographic tokens for controlling inter-agent communication.

title: Out of Context: How important is Local Context in Neural Program Repair?
reason: The abstract evaluates trained Transformer-based neural program-repair models and context-window allocation, but does not establish an LLM or foundation-model method within this corpus boundary.
